hook.text: Before the 1900s, everyone roasted coffee at home. Now a growing movement is bringing home roasting back.

buildup.text: Home roasters range from $50 popcorn poppers repurposed for coffee to $800 dedicated machines with digital profiles.

discovery.text: Green coffee costs 50–70% less than roasted. Home roasters get fresher coffee at lower cost—and control every variable.

twist.text: Home roasting produces significant smoke and chaff. Many home roasters work in garages, on balconies, or under range hoods.

climax.text: Online communities share green bean sources, roast profiles, and cupping notes. Home roasting has become a global hobby.

punchline.text: Green beans, a hot machine, and Sunday morning. Home roasting is back.

quiz.question: What is one main advantage of home coffee roasting?
options: Green coffee costs 50–70% less than roasted, with fresher results

details.summary: Home roasting has surged in popularity as affordable roasting machines and high-quality green beans became available online. Enthusiasts roast small batches for peak freshness and experiment with profiles. The community shares knowledge through forums and social media.
details.whyItMatters: Home roasting empowers coffee lovers to control freshness and flavor while deepening their understanding of the bean-to-cup journey.
takeaways: Affordable machines and online green bean sourcing fueled the trend
Home roasters enjoy peak freshness within days of roasting
Online communities share profiles, tips, and green bean reviews

faq.question: What equipment does a beginner need to start home roasting coffee?
faq.answer: A basic home roaster like the FreshRoast SR540 or a simple popcorn popper, a kitchen scale, and a source of quality green beans are all you need. Costs start around 50 to 150 dollars for entry-level setups.

faq.question: Is home-roasted coffee really better than store-bought coffee?
faq.answer: Freshness is the main advantage. Home-roasted coffee brewed within a week of roasting has more aromatic complexity than beans that may have sat on a shelf for months. Skill development takes time, but results improve quickly.
